library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Cagnardi_2017_meloxicam_buffalo"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Cagnardi_2017_meloxicam_buffalo"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0187252>
* Supporting information S1 (raw data, including the Figure 2 mean profile):
  <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0187252.s001>

Cagnardi 2017 studied the analgesic efficacy and pharmacokinetics of
meloxicam given intravenously to Mediterranean buffalo calves after
surgical castration. Only the pharmacokinetics were modelled: the clinical
endpoints (respiratory rate, heart rate, rectal temperature, pain score and
serum cortisol) were compared between treated and control calves by
repeated-measures ANOVA and rank tests, with no concentration-effect model,
so there is no pharmacodynamic layer to package.

# Population

Ten healthy male buffalo calves (3-4 months old in the Methods, median 3.65
months; the abstract says 4-5 months; 127-135 kg, median 130 kg) from one
farm in the Caserta district of southern Italy were castrated under
dexmedetomidine sedation and lidocaine local anaesthesia. Six calves (the
treated group) received a single intravenous bolus of meloxicam 0.5 mg/kg
immediately after surgery; the other four were untreated controls.
Meloxicam was measured in serum by HPLC-UV (LOQ 0.01 ug/mL) from 5 min to
96 h after dosing. Each treated calf was fitted separately with a classical
two-compartment model in WinNonlin, and Table 2 reports the mean and SD of
the six individual estimates.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Cagnardi_2017_meloxicam_buffalo")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lvc` (V1) | log(40.51) mL/kg | Table 2, row 'V1' (mean of 6 individual fits; SD 15.16) |
| `lcl` (ClB) | log(4.38) mL/h/kg | Table 2, row 'ClB' (SD 0.95) |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(101.8) mL/kg | Table 2, row 'V2' (SD 67.31) |
| `lq` | log(169.33) mL/h/kg | Derived: Table 2 'K12' 4.18 1/h x 'V1' 40.51 mL/kg |
| `propSd` | fixed(0) | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic analysis': weights 1/Yhat^2 (proportional), magnitude not reported |
| Two-compartment structure, IV bolus into central | n/a | Methods 'Pharmacokinetic analysis'; Results 'Meloxicam concentrations and pharmacokinetic analysis' |
| Dose 0.5 mg/kg IV | 500 ug/kg | Methods 'Drugs administration and surgical procedure' |
| Mean observed profile (validation target) | n/a | Figure 2; Supporting information S1, 'Meloxicam mean concentrations reported in Figure 2' |

# Secondary parameters against Table 2

The packaged model is deterministic (no between-animal variability), so its
secondary parameters follow in closed form from the four disposition
parameters. Table 2 is a table of means of individual estimates, which are
not mutually consistent: the mean of each ratio is not the ratio of the
means. The packaged set uses the means of the three parameters that
determine exposure and the extent of distribution (V1, ClB and V2) and
derives the intercompartmental clearance from mean K12 x mean V1.

```{r secondary}
mod <- readModelDb("Cagnardi_2017_meloxicam_buffalo")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- setNames(ui$iniDf$est, ui$iniDf$name)

two_cmt_secondary <- function(vc, cl, vp, q, dose = 500) {
  k10 <- cl / vc
  k12 <- q / vc
  k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  alpha <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  c(
    auc = dose / cl,
    half_k10 = log(2) / k10,
    half_alpha = log(2) / alpha,
    half_beta = log(2) / beta,
    k10 = k10,
    k12 = k12,
    k21 = k21,
    c0 = dose / vc,
    mrt = (vc + vp) / cl,
    vss = vc + vp,
    vz = cl / beta
  )
}

pk <- two_cmt_secondary(
  vc = exp(th[["lvc"]]),
  cl = exp(th[["lcl"]]),
  vp = exp(th[["lvp"]]),
  q = exp(th[["lq"]])
)

table2 <- c(
  auc = 118.81, half_k10 = 6.93, half_alpha = 0.09, half_beta = 21.51,
  k10 = 0.13, k12 = 4.18, k21 = 1.75, c0 = 14.39, mrt = 32.89,
  vss = 142.31, vz = 146.16
)
labels <- c(
  auc = "AUC0-inf (h*ug/mL)", half_k10 = "t1/2 K10 (h)",
  half_alpha = "t1/2 alpha (h, harmonic mean)",
  half_beta = "t1/2 beta (h, harmonic mean)", k10 = "K10 (1/h)",
  k12 = "K12 (1/h)", k21 = "K21 (1/h)", c0 = "C0 (ug/mL)", mrt = "MRT (h)",
  vss = "Vdss (mL/kg)", vz = "Vz (mL/kg)"
)

secondary <- tibble(
  parameter = labels[names(table2)],
  model = signif(pk[names(table2)], 4),
  table2 = table2,
  pct_diff = round(100 * (pk[names(table2)] / table2 - 1), 1)
)

secondary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter,
    "Packaged model" = model,
    "Table 2 mean" = table2,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Secondary parameters implied by the packaged model vs. the Table 2 means of the six individual fits.")

# Vdss = V1 + V2 holds exactly for the Table 2 means; AUC and MRT, which
# depend only on V1, ClB and V2, land within 4% and 2%.
stopifnot(
  abs(pk[["vss"]] / 142.31 - 1) < 0.001,
  abs(pk[["auc"]] / 118.81 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(pk[["mrt"]] / 32.89 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(pk[["vz"]] / 146.16 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(pk[["half_beta"]] / 21.51 - 1) < 0.10
)
```

The rows that differ most are the ones Table 2 summarises from skewed
individual values. Mean K10 (0.13 1/h, SD 0.09) is 20% above mean ClB /
mean V1, and mean C0 (14.39 ug/mL, SD 7.13) is 17% above dose / mean V1;
both are means of ratios whose individual values vary widely. The two
half-lives are harmonic means, which sit below the half-life of the mean
rate constant: the distribution half-life implied by the means (0.12 h,
about 7 min) is 30% longer than the 0.09 h harmonic mean (pseudo-SD
0.06 h), a difference confined to the first few minutes after the dose. With ClB = 4.38 mL/h/kg and Vdss = 142.31 mL/kg the
terminal half-life can never be shorter than ln(2) x Vdss / ClB = 22.5 h,
whatever the intercompartmental clearance, so the 21.51 h harmonic mean is
not reachable from the other means and is not used as a fitting target.

## Choice of intercompartmental clearance

For each calf Q = K12 x V1 = K21 x V2 exactly, but the means of those
products are not reported. The two available products of means are
169.33 mL/h/kg (K12 x V1, packaged) and 178.15 mL/h/kg (K21 x V2). They
differ only in the speed of the 6-7 minute distribution phase:

```{r q-choice}
t_obs <- c(0.08, 0.16, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96)
ev_q <- rxode2::et(amt = 500, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(t_obs, cmt = "central")

sim_q169 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_q)
sim_q178 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_q, params = c(lq = log(1.75 * 101.8)))
q_diff <- 100 * (sim_q178$Cc / sim_q169$Cc - 1)
knitr::kable(
  tibble(time = sim_q169$time, Cc_q169 = signif(sim_q169$Cc, 4),
         Cc_q178 = signif(sim_q178$Cc, 4), pct = round(q_diff, 1)) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Time (h)" = time,
      "Cc, Q = 169.33 (ug/mL)" = Cc_q169,
      "Cc, Q = 178.15 (ug/mL)" = Cc_q178,
      "Difference (%)" = pct
    ),
  caption = "Typical-value concentrations under the two candidate intercompartmental clearances."
)
stopifnot(max(abs(q_diff)) < 3)
```

# Replicate Figure 2

Supporting information S1 lists the mean and SD of the six calves'
concentrations at each sampling time (the column header there reads
'mg/mL'; the article text and Figure 2 give the same numbers in ug/mL).
The packaged typical-value profile is overlaid.

```{r figure-2}
fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~mean, ~sd,
  0.08, 9.392, 2.391,
  0.16, 8.030, 2.549,
  0.25, 6.164, 2.012,
  0.5, 4.426, 1.976,
  0.75, 3.806, 1.783,
  1, 3.906, 2.030,
  1.5, 3.718, 1.362,
  2, 3.438, 0.741,
  4, 3.330, 0.969,
  6, 2.558, 0.522,
  8, 2.266, 0.503,
  12, 2.238, 0.712,
  24, 1.878, 0.530,
  36, 1.278, 0.291,
  48, 0.916, 0.315,
  72, 0.264, 0.151,
  96, 0.184, 0.136
)

t_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2, 96, by = 0.5), fig2$time)))
ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = 500, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(t_grid, cmt = "central")
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_typ) |> as.data.frame()

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = sim_typ, aes(time, Cc), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_pointrange(
    data = fig2,
    aes(time, mean, ymin = pmax(mean - sd, 0.01), ymax = mean + sd)
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Meloxicam serum concentration (ug/mL)",
    title = "Figure 2 - mean (SD) observed profile and typical-value prediction",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Cagnardi 2017 (points: S1 mean +/- SD; line: packaged model)."
  )

pred_at_obs <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% fig2$time) |>
  dplyr::select(time, Cc)
fig2_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(fig2, pred_at_obs, by = "time") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc / mean - 1))
stopifnot(nrow(fig2_cmp) == nrow(fig2))

fig2_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = signif(Cc, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time (h)" = time,
    "Observed mean (ug/mL)" = mean,
    "Observed SD (ug/mL)" = sd,
    "Typical prediction (ug/mL)" = Cc,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value prediction vs. the Figure 2 mean profile.")

# The typical-value line is not a fit to the mean profile; it follows from the
# means of the individual parameters. It sits within about 15% of the mean
# observed concentration at most times; the 72 h mean (0.264 ug/mL) lies
# below the log-linear trend through its neighbours and is the one large
# outlier.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(fig2_cmp$pct_diff)) < 15,
  median(abs(fig2_cmp$pct_diff)) < 15
)
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA of the typical-value profile, sampled on a fine grid out to 96 h (the
last sampling time of the study). `cl.obs`, `vss.obs` and `mrt.obs` use the
intravascular dose; the per-kg dose makes clearance mL/h/kg and volume
mL/kg.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "0.5 mg/kg IV") |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)

dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1L, treatment = "0.5 mg/kg IV", time = 0, amt = 500)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                             route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE,
  cl.obs = TRUE, mrt.obs = TRUE, vss.obs = TRUE, vz.obs = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = "0.5 mg/kg IV",
  aucinf.obs = 118.81, half.life = 21.51,
  cl.obs = 4.38, mrt.obs = 32.89, vss.obs = 142.31, vz.obs = 146.16
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(
    aucinf.obs = "h*ug/mL", half.life = "h",
    cl.obs = "mL/h/kg", mrt.obs = "h", vss.obs = "mL/kg", vz.obs = "mL/kg"
  ),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "NCA of the typical-value profile vs. Table 2 (means of six individual fits). * differs from reference by >20%."
)

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

# Deterministic checks: NCA of the solved profile must recover the model's own
# closed-form AUC and clearance (the 96 h window leaves about 5% of the AUC to
# extrapolation) and the half-life of the terminal phase.
stopifnot(
  abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs / pk[["auc"]] - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(nca_wide$cl.obs / exp(th[["lcl"]]) - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(nca_wide$half.life / pk[["half_beta"]] - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs / 118.81 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

No row differs from Table 2 by more than 20%. C0 is compared in the
secondary-parameter table above, where it is the largest
exposure difference (-14%): dose / mean V1 is 12.3 ug/mL against a mean
individual C0 of 14.39 ug/mL (SD 7.13). A mean of individual C0 values
exceeds the dose divided by the mean volume whenever the volumes vary
(Jensen's inequality), and V1 varied with a CV of 37% across the six
calves.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Two-stage source, not a population fit.** Table 2 reports the mean and
  SD of six individual WinNonlin fits. No population typical values,
  between-animal variances or residual-error magnitude exist; the model is
  packaged as a fixed-parameter typical calf with no random effects and the
  proportional residual SD fixed at 0 (the individual fits were weighted by
  1/Yhat^2, i.e. a proportional error structure). The Table 2 SDs (CV 37%
  for V1, 22% for ClB, 66% for V2) describe the spread of six individual
  estimates and are not encoded as between-animal variances.
- **Which Table 2 means are used.** Means of individual estimates are not
  mutually consistent, so not all can be reproduced at once. The packaged
  model uses mean V1, ClB and V2, which reproduce the Table 2 Vdss exactly
  and AUC, MRT and Vz within 4%. Mean K10 (which would give CL =
  5.27 mL/h/kg and an AUC 20% low) and mean C0 are not used.
- **Intercompartmental clearance derived.** Q is not printed. It is taken
  as mean K12 x mean V1 = 169.33 mL/h/kg; the alternative mean K21 x mean
  V2 = 178.15 mL/h/kg changes no concentration at the sampling times by more
  than 3% (table above).
- **Half-lives.** Table 2 gives harmonic means of the individual half-lives
  (21.51 h terminal, 0.09 h distribution). The packaged model's terminal
  half-life is 22.8 h; no choice of Q can bring it below 22.5 h with the
  mean ClB and Vdss.
- **Per-kg parameterisation.** All volumes and clearances are per kg body
  weight as published, so doses are entered in ug/kg (0.5 mg/kg = 500
  ug/kg). There is no body-weight covariate; the calves weighed 127-135 kg.
- **Supplement unit label.** Supporting information S1 headers the mean
  meloxicam concentrations as 'mg/mL'; the Results text gives the same
  numbers (9.39, 3.81, 0.18) in ug/mL, which is also the unit of the assay
  calibration range and of Figure 2. ug/mL is used.
- **Age.** The abstract says 4-5 months; Methods say 3 and 4 months with a
  median of 3.65 months. The Methods values are carried in the population
  metadata.
- **No pharmacodynamic model.** The clinical endpoints and serum cortisol
  were analysed statistically only; no concentration-effect relationship
  was estimated, so none is packaged.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC
  or on the journal site (checked 2026-11-25).
